Heather — adding the operational detail you asked for. See inline answers and the attached brief runbook.

On retention: our data flow partitions telemetry by tenant id. For BYOK tenants the telemetry blobs are encrypted with tenant-specific envelope keys; KEKs (customer-managed) are referenced via wrapped metadata only and never exported. Retention controls:
- Default: 13 months (write-once index, immutable audit index for 90 days before archival).
- Optional contractual override: 1 month, 13 months, or 36 months.

On shift logs and operator controls:
- HSM shift logs include: shift_id, event_ts (UTC), event_type (seal/unseal/rotate/operator-login), operator_hash (sha256 salted), location id.
- Operator access uses MFA + ephemeral operator certificates with 1-hour validity. We rotate operator cert signing keys every 90 days.
- Sealing/unsealing events are accompanied by dual-approval for production HSM zones (2-of-3 operator consensus).

On rotation sample semantics: the attached rotation_sample.log.txt is a sanitized JSONL extract: each line contains rotation_id, key_id, timestamp, action (rotate_start/rotate_commit/rollback), wrapped_kek_sha256, manifest_ref. Keys are rotated using atomic double-write pattern with overlap period to allow in-flight token validation.

On transit wrapping: as Karthik noted, our TLS 1.3 mTLS path is AEAD-based. For BYOK flows we additionally wrap ephemeral session KEKs with customer KEK at rest — that metadata is sufficient for audit and cannot decrypt traffic without tenant KEK.

We have also included a short statement for your SIG/CAIQ appendix that you can drop into the questionnaire answer: a one-paragraph description of BYOK telemetry handling and rotation process. If you want more redaction or different formats (syslog vs JSONL), tell us.
